🥔じゃがいもが安い日、もうこれ一択🥔
包丁なし【お惣菜のポテトサラダ】！
包丁いらない・鍋いらない、レンジで作るポテサラです✨

▼材料（作りやすい分量）
・じゃがいも 3個（300g）
・マヨネーズ 大さじ3
・酢 小さじ1
・砂糖 ひとつまみ
・塩・こしょう 少々
・ハム 3枚
（あればコーン缶 大さじ3）

▼作り方（3工程）
①じゃがいもを洗い、ぬれたまま1個ずつラップで包んで600W 6分（竹串がスッと通ればOK）
②ふきんで持って皮を手でむき、熱いうちにフォークでつぶす。酢・砂糖・塩こしょうを混ぜる
③粗熱がとれたら、マヨと手でちぎったハム（コーン）を混ぜる

※芽と緑色の部分は、スプーンでしっかり取り除いてね
※熱いうちに酢を混ぜると、お店っぽい味になります
冷蔵で2日。サンドイッチやお弁当にも🙆‍♀️

【保存】しておくと、じゃがいもが安い日にすぐ作れます📌

⚠️持病のある方・治療中の方へ
4毒抜きは、ゆるくではなく、しっかり取り組んでほしいと思っています。自己判断ではなく、主治医に相談しながら進めてね。

▼お惣菜の日のゆるいルール4つ

②副菜は1品だけ作る（作り置きでもOK）
③ごはんは家で炊く

🥬キャベツが安い日、もうこれ一択🥬
重ねてレンジ【巻かない ロールキャベツ】！
包丁いらない・火を使わない、巻かずに重ねるだけです✨

▼材料（2〜3人分）
・キャベツ 1/4個（葉6〜8枚）
・合いびき肉 200g
・片栗粉 大さじ1
・塩・こしょう 少々
・水 200ml
・コンソメ 1個
（あれば冷凍のみじん切り玉ねぎ 50g）

▼作り方（3工程）
①ポリ袋にひき肉・片栗粉・塩こしょう（玉ねぎ）を入れて、よくもむ
②深めの耐熱ボウルに、キャベツの葉→肉だね→キャベツ…と交互に重ねる（最後はキャベツ）
③水とコンソメを入れ、ふんわりラップで600W 10分。そのまま5分おく

※真ん中の肉の色が赤ければ、1分ずつ追加してね
※ケチャップを大さじ2足すと、トマト味になります
冷蔵で3日。スープごと温め直してどうぞ🙆‍♀️

【保存】しておくと、キャベツが安い日にすぐ作れます📌

🍎りんごが安い日、もうこれ一択🍎
レンジだけ【砂糖も油もなし りんごチップス】！
包丁いらない・揚げない、りんごだけのおやつです✨

▼材料（作りやすい分量）
・りんご 1個
（あればシナモン 少々）

▼作り方（3工程）
①りんごをよく洗い、皮ごとスライサーで1〜2mmに薄切り。芯の手前まででOK、種があれば手でとる
②クッキングシートに重ならないように並べ、ラップなしで500W 4分
③裏返して2〜3分。そのあとは30秒ずつ、ふちが乾くまで加熱する

※焦げやすいので、最後はレンジの前で様子を見てね
※加熱直後はしんなり、冷めるとパリッとします
※1回に並ぶ分ずつ、数回に分けて作ってね
湿気やすいので、密閉袋で2〜3日。油・小麦・乳製品・砂糖なしのおやつです🙆‍♀️

【保存】しておくと、りんごが安い日にすぐ作れます📌

朝は時間もないし、ラクなのがいちばんなんだよね。

▼朝のパンのゆるいルール4つ
①パンは1枚だけにする
②りんごなど、果物を添える
③スープかみそ汁を1杯つける
④週に何回か、ごはんの日も作る

Hello from the start of the road.

In 1833, Hiroshige published his prints of the Tokaido, the great highway between Edo (today's Tokyo) and Kyoto. Every journey began here, at Nihonbashi: a lord's procession on the arch at dawn, fish sellers jostling below, one stray dog trotting in.

Swipe for the same bridge today. An expressway overhead, a porter with a hand truck of parcels, and a dog that still crosses as if it owns the place.

We kept Hiroshige's composition and changed the travelers. The coloring is up to you.

Follow along. We're walking all 55 views, and there are free printable pages at the link in our bio.

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

Same river, about two centuries apart.

In Hiroshige's Fuchu, there was no bridge over the Abe River. You crossed on a porter's shoulders.

Today broad bridges span the water, so the shallows belong to families. A father wades in with his daughter on his shoulders, her brother chases fish with a net, and Grandma keeps watch from the shade.

Station 20 of 55. See the rest at the link in our bio.

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

Look at the umbrella on the right.

Shono was a small, quiet stop, yet Hiroshige gave it one of the most admired prints in the whole series: a sudden summer downpour. And on that umbrella he wrote a sly plug for the publisher and the series itself.

Swipe: same hill, same cloudburst, today. A mom in a polka-dot poncho pushing her bike uphill, a student holding an umbrella like a shield, and one parcel that must stay dry.

This page is one of our free printables. Link in bio.

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

A look inside.

Every drawing faces Hiroshige's original print and a short note on what the place was like then and what it is like now. The back of every drawing is left blank.

Volume 1 runs from Nihonbashi in Tokyo to Fukuroi. Volume 2 goes on from Mitsuke to Kyoto.

The New Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō. Find it on Amazon (link in bio).

#adultcoloringbook #coloringforadults #japaneseart #ukiyoe #hiroshige #cozycoloring #japanlover

One for a December weekend.

Hiroshige's Kambara is one of the most admired snow scenes in Japanese art. A sleeping village, flakes drifting from a dark sky. The irony is that this mild stretch of coast seldom sees snow like this. Imagined or not, the silence is perfect.

Our version keeps the slope and the hush. A walker under a clear umbrella, a father in a knit cap pulling a child on a sled, snow on the parked car.

If you color this one: keep most of the page white.

#wintercoloring #adultcoloring #coloringpages #ukiyoe #hiroshige #japaneseart #cozycoloring

Some things never change. Somebody is always being dragged somewhere.

Goyu was famous for the persistence of its inn touts, and Hiroshige plays it as slapstick. One grips a man by his bundle, another by his hat cord.

The old townhouses still line the street. The touts have retired. The tugging is now done by two children and a row of capsule toy machines.

Station 36 of 55. Tag the dad.

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

Hiroshige's prints were made with surprisingly few colors.

These eight are enough to make a page look like a woodblock print: Prussian blue, crimson, vermilion orange, ochre, verdigris green, wisteria, gray, and ink black.

Two favorites from the list. Crimson: use it sparingly, a touch pulls the page together. Black: the less you add, the more elegant the page.

Save this, then pull eight pencils out of the box and see how far they go. Free pages to try them on: link in bio.

#coloringtips #adultcoloring #coloredpencil #ukiyoe #woodblockprint #hiroshige #japaneseart

Crossing the Tenryu River used to take two boats. The river split in two, so you got out, trudged across a sandbar, and waited for the next one. Look past Hiroshige's boatmen and you can see people doing exactly that.

Today a highway bridge carries the trucks over in seconds, and the wide stony banks have become a weekend picnic ground. Grandpa turns corn on the grill. His grandson waits with a plate.

Indigo for the river, bright yellow for the corn.

Station 29 of 55, and the first page of Volume 2.

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

Hiroshige let Mt. Fuji break right through the top border of the print. Too big for the picture.

Our Hara keeps the giant mountain and the cranes, now gliding over young rice, and adds a bullet train on its viaduct, a farmer by a vending machine, and a mom pedaling past with a child in the back seat.

Coloring note from the book: leave Fuji's slopes pale. A single band of blue sky will do.

This is one of 28 drawings in Volume 1 of The New Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō. Find it on Amazon (link in bio).

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

A little road trivia.

For travelers walking west to Kyoto, Mt. Fuji usually rose on the right. But near Yoshiwara the road bends, and for a short stretch it shows up on the left. Hiroshige framed that famous left-hand Fuji between pine trunks, with three children riding together on one horse.

Swipe to the last slide: our three young riders are toddlers in a nursery outing cart. Fuji is, sure enough, on the left.

Have you seen Fuji from the train? Which side were you on?

#japantravel #japantrip #oldjapan #tokaido #ukiyoe #woodblockprint #hiroshige

Hiroshige plainly enjoyed this one.

Two sumo wrestlers crossing the Okitsu River. One on a straining horse, the other crammed into a palanquin carried by porters who look ready to sink.

The hills around Okitsu are mandarin country now, so our heavy load rides on a small truck piled high with crates of fruit.

Save your brightest orange for this page.

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

What's inside, for those who asked.

Each spread pairs Hiroshige's original print with the same view today, drawn in line for you to color. A short note tells you what the place was like then and what it is like now, and often ends with a color hint ("Save your brightest orange for this page").

The back of every drawing is left blank. At the front: the eight colors of ukiyo-e and five simple rules for using them.

The New Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, in two volumes. Find it on Amazon (link in bio).

#adultcoloringbook #coloringforadults #japaneseart #ukiyoe #hiroshige #cozycoloring #japanlover

Hiroshige's Yokkaichi is all wind.

A willow thrashing, a traveler bent double inside his cape, and a man lunging after his straw hat. Look at the lower left of the print: the hat is still rolling, a step ahead of him, forever.

The gale is the same today. So is the chase.

Station 44 of 55.

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

You know the one. Came home with a suitcase of snacks and has been planning the next trip ever since.

This might be their kind of gift: Hiroshige's famous road from Tokyo to Kyoto, redrawn with the travelers of today, to color one quiet evening at a time. Every drawing faces the original print.

Add a box of colored pencils and you're done.

The New Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, Volumes 1 and 2. Find it on Amazon (link in bio), and do check the delivery date before you order.

#giftsforjapanlovers #holidaygiftideas #coloringbook #adultcoloring #japaneseart #hiroshige

For the dog people.

Each early summer Chiryu held a famous horse fair. Hiroshige filled the meadow with horses grazing at their stakes, while the dealers gathered in the shade of a lone pine to haggle.

Horse fairs are long gone from Chiryu. But every morning the riverbank fills with four-legged company of another kind.

If you colored this page, which dog would be yours?

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

Snow is rare in Hiroshige's Tokaido, which makes Kameyama sparkle. The morning has cleared, the sky glows pink, and the bearers' hats look ready to slide back down the hill.

Our climbers wear puffy coats and boots. A snowman keeps watch. One child has wisely chosen the sled.

Leave plenty of white, and touch the sky with pink.

From Volume 2 of The New Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō. Find it on Amazon (link in bio).

#wintercoloring #adultcoloring #coloringpages #ukiyoe #hiroshige #japaneseart #cozycoloring

Hiroshige stopped for lunch.

In his Mariko, two travelers sit at a thatched teahouse. The sign out front advertises the local specialty, tororo-jiru: grated mountain yam poured over rice.

A thatched restaurant beside the bridge in Mariko has been serving it since 1596. It still does.

Our drawing looks out from the tatami room as a server brings a wooden tub of barley rice. The plum tree is just coming into bloom, so: plum pink, please.

Would you try it?

#japantravel #japantrip #oldjapan #tokaido #ukiyoe #woodblockprint #hiroshige

Volume 2 is the second half of the road: from the ferry at Mitsuke, past castle towns, a festival night, a windy riverbank and a snowy hill, to the Sanjo Bridge in Kyoto.

Same idea as Volume 1. Hiroshige's original print on one page, the same view today on the facing page, yours to color.

The New Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, Volume 2. Find it on Amazon (link in bio).

#adultcoloringbook #coloringforadults #japaneseart #ukiyoe #hiroshige #cozycoloring #japanlover

A thank-you to everyone carrying boxes this week.

Every post town on the Tokaido kept a relay office where fresh porters and horses took over the loads. Hiroshige's Fujieda shows the handover in full swing: porters wiping their sweat and stretching their backs, officials checking the paperwork.

The baton has passed to the delivery depot. Reflective jackets, a hand truck, someone sitting down for a breather, vans waiting in the yard.

Station 23 of 55.

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

The longest nights of the year deserve this one.

Hiroshige's Kambara, then ours. Same slope, same hush.

This page is one of our free printables. Print it, put the kettle on, and keep most of the page white. Link in bio.

#wintercoloring #adultcoloring #coloringpages #ukiyoe #hiroshige #japaneseart #cozycoloring

If you only borrow one trick from Hiroshige, borrow this.

Look at the sky in his prints. Only the top edge is a deep indigo. Then it fades to white as it comes down.

Do that on any landscape page and it starts to look like a woodblock print. Press hard along the top, lighten your hand as you go, and stop sooner than you think.

Save this for your next sky.

#coloringtips #adultcoloring #coloredpencil #ukiyoe #woodblockprint #hiroshige #japaneseart

A darker story for a dark evening.

Between Kanaya and Nissaka lay a pass so steep that Hiroshige's road seems to tilt off the page. In the middle of the path sits a round boulder: the Night-Weeping Stone. Legend says it cried out after a pregnant woman was murdered on the pass, so that her baby was found and saved.

In our drawing the travelers are high school students walking home, one pushing a bicycle uphill, with the round stone resting at the edge of the road.

Do you know a place with a legend like this?

#japantravel #japantrip #oldjapan #tokaido #ukiyoe #woodblockprint #hiroshige

Find the servant with his arms flung high. He is plainly bored of the crossing.

The boat ride across the lake ended at Arai, home of a strict checkpoint whose building, remarkably, still stands. Hiroshige gives the lord a grand barge with streamers snapping in the wind, and gives the servants a yawn.

Small boats carry visitors across the water again today. Color the flags vermilion and let the wind do the rest.

Station 32 of 55.

#hiroshige #ukiyoe #adultcoloring #coloringbook #japantravel #tokaido #thenandnow

However you are spending tonight, we hope it is peaceful.

If you would like something quiet to do with your hands, our snowy night page is free to print. A hillside village, a walker under an umbrella, a child on a sled. Most of it stays white.

Link in bio. Warm wishes from the old road.

#wintercoloring #adultcoloring #coloringpages #ukiyoe #hiroshige #japaneseart #cozycoloring

Keeping warm, then and now.

Hiroshige gathers a few farmers around a fire at the foot of one enormous tree, its smoke climbing higher than the trunk. A traveler in a wide straw hat stops to share the heat.

Our fire is a dondo-yaki, the January bonfire where New Year decorations go up in smoke and children toast rice cakes on bamboo poles.

Wherever you are today, we hope you're somewhere warm.

#wintercoloring #adultcoloring #coloringpages #ukiyoe #hiroshige #japaneseart #cozycoloring

If the gift you really wanted was a quiet hour, here is an idea for the new year.

Walk Hiroshige's road from Tokyo to Kyoto, one page at a time. No schedule. The drawings keep his compositions and swap in the travelers of today, and each one faces the original print with a short note on the place.

Not sure where to start with color? The front of the book gives you the eight colors of ukiyo-e and five simple rules.

The New Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō. Find it on Amazon (link in bio).

#adultcoloringbook #coloringforadults #japaneseart #ukiyoe #hiroshige #cozycoloring #japanlover

Hiroshige makes the flat land feel fast: bearers jogging home with an empty palanquin, a lone porter hurrying the other way.

Every January this road sees a different kind of runner. Hiratsuka is a relay point of the Hakone Ekiden, the great college relay between Tokyo and Hakone. Our runner sprints by with a camera bike close behind, as a volunteer sets out cups of water.

The hill and Fuji watch it all, unhurried as ever.

From Volume 1 of The New Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō. Find it on Amazon (link in bio).

#japantravel #japantrip #oldjapan #tokaido #ukiyoe #woodblockprint #hiroshige

The old printers had a golden rule: large areas pale, small areas strong.

Kakegawa is the perfect page to try it. In Hiroshige's print, a child gapes after a kite whose string has snapped, sailing away above the rice fields. In ours the kite is held fast.

Keep the winter sky and the fields pale. Then give the kite your brightest vermilion. One small strong spot, and the whole page wakes up.

What's your one bright color?

#coloringtips #adultcoloring #coloredpencil #ukiyoe #woodblockprint #hiroshige #japaneseart

A New Year tradition from Japan.

In January, the New Year decorations are burned on a bonfire called dondo-yaki, and children toast rice cakes over it on long bamboo poles.

We drew one into our version of Hamamatsu, where Hiroshige's farmers once warmed their hands beneath a giant tree. The castle is still on the horizon, now joined by a tall city tower.

Does your family have a New Year tradition? Tell us below.

#japantravel #japantrip #oldjapan #tokaido #ukiyoe #woodblockprint #hiroshige

A year is a good length for a long walk.

Start at Nihonbashi. Finish at the Sanjo Bridge in Kyoto, where the last note in the book says: color this one slowly.

Thank you for walking with us this month. Next up: the runners of January.

The New Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō, Volumes 1 and 2. Find it on Amazon (link in bio).

肉じゃがに、うちはこれを入れるって具ある？

うちはしらたきじゃなくて、ちくわ。
子どもの頃からずっとこれ。

かぼちゃは切る前にレンジで2分。

皮がやわらかくなって
包丁がすっと入る。

かぼちゃの煮物、甘め派？しょっぱめ派？

うちは砂糖なしで、白だしだけ。
かぼちゃの甘さで十分。

冬になると冷蔵庫に常備してるもの、教えてほしい。

うちは白菜の浅漬け。
塩昆布ともむだけ。

鍋のしめ、ぶっちゃけ何派？

うちはごはんでも麺でもなく、
おもちを入れる。

キャベツの芯は捨てない。

薄く切ってみそ汁へ。
甘くてやわらかくなる。

キャベツが半玉残ったら、まず何にする？
